newsitem.title: USA: NY Senate backs cost-of-living rise for lawmakers.
newsitem.headline: NY Senate backs cost-of-living rise for lawmakers.

text.p: The New York Senate Majority Leader said Tuesday that while he would not support a pay raise for lawmakers and other state officials, he would support a cost-of-living increase.
Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, who also said he had never in his life supported a pay raise for legislators, made the comments at a gathering of the New York State Newspaper Publishers Association in Albany.

The controversial pay issue resurfaced amid suggestions that Gov. George Pataki had proposed raising the base pay of Albany's lawmakers, who have not had a raise since 1989, to around $75,000 from the present $57,500 -- in return for their agreeing to approve a budget on time.
New York State's budget is due on April 1, and the state for 12 years in a row has failed to meet this deadline.
Pataki, at a separate news conference, told reporters in Albany that the pay issue was not now being negotiated, though he urged any talks not be kept secret.
"To the extent there is any discusion, I think it should be done in the open and in the light of day, but its's not something we're looking at at this point."
Pataki reminded reporters that under state law, no sitting legislature can raise its own pay, so the earliest session that would get the benefit of any rise would be a newly elected body in 1999.
A spokeswoman for Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, was not immediately available to comment.
